'''Rodney Carney''' (born [[April 15]], [[1984]] in [[Indianapolis, Indiana|Indianapolis]], [[Indiana]]) is an [[United States|American]] [[basketball]] player who recently finished his [[college basketball|college]] career at the [[University of Memphis]]. Carney is a senior [[small forward]] whom most mock drafts project as a [[NBA Draft Lottery|lottery]] pick in the [[2006 NBA Draft]]. [http://nbadraft.net/index.asp] [http://www.collegehoopsnet.com/Draft/mockdraft.htm] [http://probasketball.about.com/od/nbadraft/l/bl_mockdraft_a.htm]

==High school==
While at [[Northwest High School (Indianapolis, Indiana)|Northwest High School]], ''[[The Indianapolis Star]]'' named Carney as Player of the Year. He also made the Indiana all-star team. Outside of basketball, Carney was the Indiana state [[high jump]] champion in his senior year, with a personal best of 6'11".

==Early college career==
Carney made the [[Conference USA]] all-freshman team in 2002–2003, his first season at the University of Memphis. In the same season, the Tigers made their first [[2003 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] appearance since 1996, but the seventh-seeded Tigers lost in the opening round to [[Arizona State University|Arizona State]].

In 2003–2004, Carney showed improvement in his stats. He needed surgery after suffering from a cracked [[bone]] above his [[eye]], but he missed only two games. The Tigers again made it to the [[2004 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] as a seven seed and won their opening round game against [[University of South Carolina|South Carolina]] before losing in the second round against [[Oklahoma State University - Stillwater|Oklahoma State]].

Carney made all-Conference USA second team in 2004–2005. He led the Tigers in scoring (16 points per game) and [[free throw]] percentage (73.3%). This season, the Tigers could not reach the NCAA Tournament unless they won the Conference USA Tournament. The Tigers reached the final game against Louisville. They trailed 75-73 when freshman Memphis [[point guard]] [[Darius Washington Jr.]] was fouled on a 3-point shot with no time left. However, Washington made only the first free throw, and so Memphis lost. Carney had only 5 points and 3 rebounds in the game. In the 2005 [[National Invitation Tournament]], Memphis defeated [[Northeastern University, Boston|Northeastern]], [[Virginia Polytechnic Institute and State University|Virginia Tech]], and [[Vanderbilt University|Vanderbilt]] before losing in the semifinals to [[Saint Joseph's University|Saint Joseph's]].

==2005–2006 season==
In 2005–2006, Carney was on the preseason and mid-season lists for the [[John R. Wooden Award]] All-American team. Carney improved his stats again, becoming one of the top players in Conference USA. Carney, the only starting senior on the team, helped lead Memphis as one of the top-ranked teams in the country and was named the Conference USA player of the year. Memphis won the 2006 Conference USA Tournament, and entered the [[2006 NCAA Men's Division I Basketball Tournament|NCAA Tournament]] with a 30-3 record and a number one seed.

In the opening round against [[Oral Roberts University|Oral Roberts]], Carney led Memphis with 19 points and added 5 rebounds when Memphis won 94-78. In the next round, Carney scored 10 points and grabbed 4 rebounds to help Memphis beat [[Bucknell University|Bucknell]] 72-56. Against [[Bradley University|Bradley]] in the Sweet Sixteen, Carney scored 23 points, grabbed 4 rebounds, and added 3 steals to help Memphis win 80-64. Memphis was defeated by [[University of California, Los Angeles|UCLA]] in the Elite Eight, and Carney finished his collegiate career with a five point effort on 2 of 12 shooting.

Houston Rockets all-star forward Tracy McGrady helped Carney to prepare him for the 2006 NBA draft, and the Rockets hold the 8th pick in that draft.
